# Win/Loss Analysis Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Win/Loss Analysis Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 22 captured build checkpoints; 6 skills; 2 knowledge files; 6 acceptance checks; 6 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access; confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model and keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded files, proposed CRM, feedback, competitive, Power BI and Teams connectors, and channels; document blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who builds, tests and later uses the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for CRM, feedback, competitive, reporting and collaboration connections with dedicated references; the synthetic workshop needs none. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare sales operations, enablement, leadership and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: GitHub Copilot in VS Code Agent mode, the Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Scenario-assumption ownership | Have finance validate intervention costs, recovery rates and timelines before they replace the synthetic assumptions. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** How loss reasons and buyer feedback are captured and reviewed for enablement, product and investment decisions. Agree where inconsistent loss reasons and feedback leave leaders without a shared basis before attributing change to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Period | Closed opportunities | Loss reasons recorded | Feedback captured | Competitor named | Decision informed | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Sales business owner | Approve scope, loss-reason definitions, review gates and success measures; keep synthetic figures out of customer results. |
| Finance, enablement and executive reviewers | Finance validates assumptions, enablement approves content, and product, security, legal and executive reviewers approve actions within their authority. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and six skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the agent Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any sales connection is approved. |
| Sales data and connection owners | Approve CRM, feedback, competitive, Power BI and Teams access; create a dedicated connection reference for each seam. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check WL-01 through WL-06, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject duplicate or hidden-anchor evidence. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route strategy decisions to authorized reviewers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures for win/loss review are agreed.
- [ ] The business owner records how loss reasons and buyer feedback are captured today before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/win-loss-analysis/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and approved publisher prefix are recorded, with maker access granted, before any build starts.
- [ ] The authenticated sales audience and least-privilege scopes for deal and feedback data are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/win-loss-analysis/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/win-loss-analysis/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/win-loss-analysis/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/win-loss-analysis/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Win/Loss Analysis Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_win-loss-analysis-operating-rules.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_win-loss-analysis-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: action-summary
9. Add skill: board-presentation
10. Add skill: counter-strategies
11. Add skill: revenue-impact
12. Add skill: root-cause-analysis
13. Add skill: win-loss-overview
14. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
15. Open a fresh Preview conversation
16. Pass WL-01: Sales Operations Manager
17. Pass WL-02: Enablement Manager
18. Pass WL-03: Enablement Manager
19. Pass WL-04: Sales Leader
20. Pass WL-05: Sales Leader
21. Pass WL-06: Sales Operations Manager
22. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: WL-01, WL-02, WL-03, WL-04, WL-05, WL-06. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, its smoke test calls `WinLossAnalysisAgent` and returns the required markers.
- [ ] If built manually, the Draft has the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, six skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Unchanged WL-01 through WL-06 prompts pass, each in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Each case passes on its final response; duplicate or hidden-anchor frames are not proof.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing deal, account or buyer-feedback data. Request only the read scopes the approved sales sources need. Restrict the audience and test authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 Sales

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales data and connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 Sales — read:** Bind approved read-only connector actions for closed opportunities.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 Sales:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 Sales:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 Sales:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 5](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Update no CRM record; cite the synthetic loss reasons as recorded. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): State the limitation; never invent evidence.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved buyer-feedback or conversation-intelligence source

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales data and connection owners

1. **Bind Approved buyer-feedback or conversation-intelligence source — read:** Add approved feedback content as a governed knowledge source with an owner.

2. **Identity for Approved buyer-feedback or conversation-intelligence source:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved buyer-feedback or conversation-intelligence source:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved buyer-feedback or conversation-intelligence source:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Contact no buyer and change no pricing; draft counter-strategy options for review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a CRM write, message or publication succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Competitive intelligence source

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales data and connection owners

1. **Bind Competitive intelligence source — read:** Add approved competitive content as a governed knowledge source.

2. **Identity for Competitive intelligence source:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Competitive intelligence source:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Competitive intelligence source:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Contact no buyer and change no pricing; draft counter-strategy options for review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return the unsupported-input error; produce no analysis.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Power BI

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales data and connection owners

1. **Bind Power BI — read:** Query an approved curated dataset read-only with the Power BI connector.

2. **Identity for Power BI:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Power BI:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Power BI:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Return the unsupported-input limitation; only the bundled synthetic Q3 snapshot is available. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return the unsupported-input error; produce no analysis.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Microsoft Teams

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales data and connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams — write:** Gate any posting workflow behind enablement and leadership approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Publish nothing; the talk track is a draft for enablement approval. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a CRM write, message or publication succeeded.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales data and connection owners

Create dedicated connection references for the approved production seams; do not reuse ambiguous existing connections.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Dedicated connection references are bound only after the synthetic evidence route is replaced, and each binding is validated.
- [ ] No CRM write, message, publication or live lookup is claimed unless an approved production tool returns evidence of success.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as sales personas and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic win rates, costs and ROI are not production thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked win/loss corpus | All six cases, WL-01 through WL-06, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, six skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Read-only boundary | Any forecast change, spend approval, CRM write, outreach, publication or program launch is no-go. |
| Scenario labeling | Every exact value is identified as synthetic or a planning assumption, never a measured customer outcome. |
| Release state | The manual and pilot agents are Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Publication and any external action have explicit confirmation.
- [ ] The approved sales audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review win/loss sessions, failed interactions, tool authentication errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses an eligible environment type and a supported restore target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
